topics.label: Who is Jesus
topics.question: Who is Jesus?
topics.tier_note: Christians do not disagree on this
topics.framing: Everything else rests here. Jesus of Nazareth claimed to be God — not a guru, not a prophet with good advice, but the Lord of heaven and earth in person. He was either wrong, lying, or telling the truth, and the church has staked everything on the third. Before anything else, get clear on who He is: true God and true man, crucified, and bodily raised.

videos.creator: Voddie Baucham
videos.why_this_one: A sermon on the question itself: Jesus as fully God and fully man, and why nothing less can save.

videos.creator: Dallas Theological Seminary

topics.label: What happened
topics.question: What just happened to me?
topics.tier_note: Christians do not disagree on this
topics.framing: You responded to something — now let's name it. The gospel is news, not advice: Christ died for your sins, was buried, and rose on the third day. You didn't clean yourself up and earn a place; God moved toward you while you were still His enemy. What happened is called grace, and the rest of your life is learning how deep it goes.

videos.title: Sanctification: The Believer’s Transformation, Part 1
videos.creator: Grace to You
videos.why_this_one: John MacArthur names the change itself: conversion doesn't just forgive you, it makes you new — and the transformation now underway is the evidence something real happened.

videos.title: Sanctification: The Believer’s Transformation, Part 2
videos.creator: Grace to You
videos.why_this_one: Part 2 carries the argument forward: how God actually works the change in you — not by your willpower, but by His Spirit, over a lifetime.

videos.title: The Doctrine of Regeneration
videos.creator: Voddie Baucham
videos.why_this_one: The word for what just happened is regeneration — the new birth. Baucham shows it is God's doing from first to last: you didn't turn over a new leaf, you were made alive.

topics.label: The resurrection
topics.question: Did the resurrection really happen?
topics.tier_note: Christians do not disagree on this
topics.framing: If Christ is not raised, your faith is worthless — the Bible itself says so. Christianity is the only faith that invites you to check its founding event as history: an empty tomb, hostile witnesses, men who died rather than recant what they saw. You are not asked to believe blindly. Look at the evidence; it holds.

topics.label: Who is God
topics.question: Who is God?
topics.tier_note: Christians do not disagree on this
topics.framing: One God, three persons — Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Not three gods, not one person wearing masks. This is the deepest mystery of the faith and also the most practical: it means God has been love from all eternity, that the Father sent the Son, and that the Spirit now lives in everyone who belongs to Him — including you.

topics.label: Trusting the Bible
topics.question: Can I trust the Bible?
topics.tier_note: Christians do not disagree on this
topics.framing: The Bible is not one book but sixty-six, written across centuries, and it is the best-attested text of the ancient world by an enormous margin. But trust is not just about manuscripts — it's about whether God has spoken. Jesus treated Scripture as God's word, and if He is who He says He is, that settles the question of authority.

topics.label: Reading the Bible
topics.question: How do I read the Bible?
topics.tier_note: Christians do not disagree on this
topics.framing: Don't start at page one and stall in Leviticus. Start with a Gospel — John or Mark — and watch Jesus. Read whole books, not fortune-cookie verses; context is everything. You will hit things you don't understand — keep going, the essentials are clear. The goal isn't finishing a reading plan. It's meeting God in what He said.

videos.title: How to Read the Bible (A Plan That Works)
videos.creator: Gavin Ortlund
videos.why_this_one: Gavin Ortlund on reading Scripture day by day: see the Bible as one story in two parts, expect its variety, and follow a plan that actually lasts.

topics.label: Prayer
topics.question: How do I pray?
topics.tier_note: Christians do not disagree on this
topics.framing: Prayer is not a performance and there are no magic words — it is a child talking to a Father who already loves you. Jesus gave a model: honor God, ask for what you need, confess, and rest in His protection. Pray badly rather than not at all. The Spirit Himself helps you when you don't know what to say — that's a promise.

videos.title: Paul Washer "On Prayer" Matthew 6:9-11
videos.creator: Paul Washer
videos.why_this_one: Paul Washer preaches on prayer from Matthew 6:9–11, the opening words of the Lord's Prayer.

videos.creator: Tim Keller
videos.why_this_one: Tim Keller shows how the Psalms teach prayer as friendship with God, and how Scripture and meditating on Christ's death help that friendship grow.

topics.label: Assurance
topics.question: Am I really saved?
topics.tier_note: Christians do not disagree on this
topics.framing: Almost every new believer asks this in the dark, and almost no one tells you it's normal. Assurance rests on what Christ did, not on the quality of your faith or the steadiness of your feelings. You are not saved by feeling saved. Look outward at the cross, not inward at your performance — He does not lose what is His.

topics.label: Still sinning
topics.question: Why do I still sin?
topics.tier_note: Christians do not disagree on this
topics.framing: Becoming a Christian did not make you sinless — it made the war start. That struggle you feel is not evidence that nothing happened; it's evidence that something did. The old you never fought back. God's Spirit is remaking you slowly, through ordinary means, with real setbacks. Repent quickly, get up again, and keep walking.

videos.title: Voddie Baucham: The World, the Flesh, and the Devil
videos.creator: Voddie Baucham
videos.why_this_one: Becoming a Christian enlists you in a war fought on three fronts. Baucham explains why the struggle that follows conversion should not surprise you.

topics.label: Church
topics.question: Do I need a church?
topics.tier_note: Christians do not disagree on this
topics.framing: You can't follow Jesus alone — not because the rules say so, but because He designed it that way. The church is not a building or a brand; it's the people He purchased, gathered to hear the word, break bread, and carry each other. Find one that preaches the Bible and loves people, and plant yourself. Imperfect is normal; absent is not.

topics.label: Suffering
topics.question: Why is there suffering?
topics.tier_note: Christians do not disagree on this
topics.framing: Christianity never pretends suffering isn't real or doesn't hurt — its center is a cross. God has not yet ended evil, but He has entered it: Jesus wept, bled, and died inside it, and rose to guarantee its end. You will not get every answer here. You will get a God who suffered with you and a promise that none of it is wasted.

topics.label: Only one way
topics.question: Isn't it arrogant to say Jesus is the only way?
topics.tier_note: Christians do not disagree on this
topics.framing: It would be arrogant — if Christians had invented the claim. But it's Jesus' own: no one comes to the Father except through Him. Every faith makes exclusive claims, including the claim that all paths are equal. The question is not which claim is humble; it's which is true. And an open door that cost God His Son is not arrogance — it's rescue.

topics.label: Family & friends
topics.question: What will my family and friends say?
topics.tier_note: Christians do not disagree on this
topics.framing: Jesus was honest about this: following Him can cost relationships, and He asked for loyalty above even family. That's not a license to be obnoxious — you're called to more patience and love toward them, not less. Some will mock, some will watch, some will follow. Hold fast, stay kind, and remember that He was rejected first.

topics.label: Baptism
topics.question: What is baptism?
topics.tier_note: That it matters is settled; how and when is honestly disputed
topics.framing: That baptism matters is not in dispute — Jesus commanded it, and the church has always obeyed. It is the public sign of belonging to Christ. But faithful Christians have honestly disagreed for centuries about how and when: believers on profession of faith, or the children of believers too. Here are both cases at their strongest. This is your first look at a question where good Christians differ — notice that it can be studied without fear.

topics.label: Disagreement
topics.question: What do Christians disagree about — and why is that alright?
topics.tier_note: How to hold everything you just learned
topics.framing: You now know the essentials — the things Christians cannot disagree on and still be Christians. Everything else on this pathway was that kind of truth. But you will soon meet believers who differ on baptism, the end times, spiritual gifts, church government — and you need to know which differences are which. Knowing which hills are worth dying on is the most useful skill a young believer can learn. In essentials, unity. In non-essentials, liberty. In all things, charity.

topics.label: Science & God
topics.question: Does science disprove God?
topics.tier_note: No — but how God created is honestly debated
topics.framing: You've been handed a story: science on one side, God on the other, pick one. That story is newer and weaker than it looks. Modern science grew up in Christian soil — pioneered largely by believers who expected an ordered universe because an ordered God made it. Science studies the world; it cannot rule on the One who made it, any more than reading a book disproves its author. Christians do debate how and how long God took in creating — you'll meet that conversation later, as an open question. But no discovery has ever reopened the tomb.
